notes: Reached via plain HTTPS fetch, no WAF; robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow. Discovery via homepage mega-menu JSON (editorialContent.content.nav) plus category-sitemap.xml grep for new/latest/just-arrived terms. The mega-menu's top-level 'New & Inspiration' department tab (categoryId key0, url /category/new) is the umbrella that also houses Christmas/Halloween/trend picks; its own sub-tile is literally labelled 'New Arrivals' and points to the same /category/new URL. Opened /category/new and confirmed it is a genuine PLP (H1 'New', Filter + Sort by + productId facet markup, canonical https://www.dunelm.com/category/new) even though its SEO <title> reads 'New Collection - Seasonal Styles | Dunelm' - the brief's 'Collection page needs inspection every time' case, resolved as genuine (not flagged) because the site's own nav names it 'New Arrivals' verbatim and it behaves exactly like every other filterable category PLP, not a lookbook/editorial page. The mega-menu also exposes 10 department-scoped 'New X' tiles (New Bedding, New Furniture, New Rugs & Doormats/New Rugs [same URL, alias], New Home Decor, New Curtains & Blinds, New Curtains, New Kitchenware, New Lighting, New Storage, New Kids). Every one of these was fetched and found to resolve to the ordinary department catalogue page - H1 'All Bedding' / 'All Furniture' / 'All Rugs' / 'All Home Decor' / 'All Curtains And Blinds' / 'All Curtains' / 'All Kitchen' / 'All Lighting' / 'All Storage' / 'All Kids' (identical title/H1 to the plain, unfiltered department page already covered by the sibling Furniture/Textile/Storage/etc. projects) with a '?highlights=new-in' query filter applied on top. These are query-filtered re-cuts of the general catalogue, not distinct New-Arrivals PLPs in their own right, so per the filter-re-cut exclusion convention they are EXCLUDED here (only the site's own dedicated /category/new hub is kept). 'New Furniture' redirects (301) to the plain /category/home-and-furniture/furniture page with no filter at all, i.e. the tile is stale/dead - further support for excluding the department tiles as non-genuine listings. No seasonal-campaign or lookbook-only page was found masquerading as New Arrivals.
